workflow.name: Silent packet loss check
workflow.description: Diagnoses traffic lost between two devices when both ports look healthy: resolves the far end of the cable via NetBox, pulls 5m Prometheus telemetry for both ends from Grafana MCP, applies fixed verdict rules, annotates the silent-loss dashboard, and emails the result. Read-only against the network — no SSH/config nodes.

device.description: Near-end device name (NetBox name / Prometheus source label).

config_overrides.body:
Workflow `{{ run.workflow_name }}` failed at step `{{ run.failed_step_id }}` with: {{ run.failed_step_error }}

Run details: {{ run.url }}
config_overrides.subject: FlowWeaver run {{ run.id }} failed - Silent packet loss check

snippets.name: email_send
snippets.description: Send an email / e-mail notification / report by mail. Delivers through a configured SMTP relay (Gmail, Microsoft 365, SendGrid, Amazon SES, Mailgun or a custom server — see /email). Use this whenever a workflow should email someone. Set `to` and `subject` in the node's config_overrides plus `body` (plain text) and/or `html`; optional `cc`, `bcc`, `reply_to` and `attachments` (base64 — feed it from an upstream `report` step). Omit `channel_id` to use the default channel. Host, port, TLS and the password live on the channel, never on the node. The send is NOT reversible. Branch on {{ steps.X.output.ok }}. Use target_mode='once' (not device-scoped).

cc.description: Optional carbon-copy recipient(s), same shape as `to`.

to.description: Recipient(s): one address, a comma-separated string, or an array of addresses.

bcc.description: Optional blind-copy recipient(s), same shape as `to`.

body.description: Plain-text body. Supply `body`, `html`, or both — at least one is required.

html.description: HTML body. When supplied alone, a plain-text alternative is generated automatically.

subject.description: Subject line. Templates like {{ steps.X.output.field }} expand before send.

from_name.description: Optional display name for the sender.

channel_id.description: Optional. The EmailChannel (SMTP relay) to send through — a UUID from /email. Omit to use the deployment's default channel.

attachments.description: Optional attachments. Feed content_base64 from an upstream `report` step to email a generated PDF/XLSX.

from_address.description: Optional override of the channel's sender. Most providers reject a From they do not own.

ok.description: TRUE only when the SMTP server accepted the message — branch on this.

error.description: SMTP failure reason when ok=false (auth rejected, TLS handshake, unreachable relay).

provider.description: gmail | outlook365 | sendgrid | ses | mailgun | smtp.

message_id.description: RFC 5322 Message-ID of the sent message.

snippets.name: mcp_call

Browse servers/tools in the builder's MCP section (or via list_mcp_servers / discover_mcp_tools). Reads {{ steps.X.output.content }} downstream. Use target_mode='once' (not device-scoped).

arguments.description: Arguments matching the tool's input schema. Templates like {{ steps.X.output.field }} expand before the call.

tool_name.description: The exact tool name on that server.

mcp_server_id.description: The registered MCP server's id (a UUID). Browse servers/tools in the builder's MCP section.

content.description: The tool's text content (MCP content blocks concatenated).

is_error.description: TRUE when the tool reported an error — branch on this.

structured.description: Optional structured payload the tool returned.

snippets.description: Shortcut verdict builder used when NetBox has no resolvable link_peers for the near-end interface.

snippets.name: silent-loss-netbox-lookup
snippets.description: Looks up the NetBox interface for the given device/interface and reads link_peers to find the far end of the cable.
snippets.code:
from flowweaver_runtime import get_input, set_output, integration, log

inp = get_input()
device = inp.get('device')
interface = inp.get('interface')
if not device or not interface:
    raise ValueError("device and interface are required inputs")

nb = integration('netbox')
resp = nb.get('/api/dcim/interfaces/', params={'device': device, 'name': interface})
if not resp.ok:
    raise RuntimeError(f"NetBox HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:300]}")

data = resp.json()
results = data.get('results') or []

if not results:
    log('warning', 'interface not found in NetBox', device=device, interface=interface)
    set_output({
        'link_found': False,
        'near_device': device,
        'near_interface': interface,
        'far_device': None,
        'far_interface': None,
        'reason': 'interface_not_found',
    })
else:
    iface = results[0]
    link_peers = iface.get('link_peers') or []
    far_device = None
    far_interface = None
    for peer in link_peers:
        if isinstance(peer, dict):
            peer_device = (peer.get('device') or {}).get('name')
            peer_name = peer.get('name')
            if peer_device and peer_name:
                far_device = peer_device
                far_interface = peer_name
                break
    link_found = bool(far_device and far_interface)
    if not link_found:
        log('warning', 'no cable/link_peers found for interface', device=device, interface=interface)
    set_output({
        'link_found': link_found,
        'near_device': device,
        'near_interface': interface,
        'far_device': far_device,
        'far_interface': far_interface,
        'reason': None if link_found else 'no_link_peers',
    })
snippets.logic_diagram_mermaid:
flowchart TD
    in([input: device, interface]) --> get[GET /api/dcim/interfaces via integration netbox]
    get --> found{results non-empty?}
    found -->|no| nf([link_found=false, reason=interface_not_found])
    found -->|yes| peers{link_peers has device+name?}
    peers -->|no| np([link_found=false, reason=no_link_peers])
    peers -->|yes| ok([link_found=true, far_device, far_interface])

snippets.name: silent-loss-compute-verdict
snippets.description: Parses the two query_prometheus responses and applies the fixed verdict rules for silent packet loss diagnosis.

snippets.name: silent-loss-finalize-verdict
snippets.description: Merges whichever verdict branch ran (compute-verdict or cable-missing-verdict) and formats the annotation text and email body.
snippets.code:
from flowweaver_runtime import get_input, set_output
import time

inp = get_input()
steps = inp.get('steps', {})

result = None
for node_id in ('compute-verdict', 'cable-missing-verdict'):
    entry = steps.get(node_id)
    if entry and entry.get('output'):
        result = entry['output']
        break

if result is None:
    raise ValueError("neither compute-verdict nor cable-missing-verdict produced an output - check the conditional wiring")

verdict = result.get('verdict', 'inconclusive')
detail = result.get('detail', '')
figures = result.get('figures') or {}

lk = (steps.get('netbox-lookup') or {}).get('output') or {}
near_device = lk.get('near_device')
near_interface = lk.get('near_interface')
far_device = lk.get('far_device')
far_interface = lk.get('far_interface')

now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)

# --- Grafana annotation text: when a loss percentage was computed, lead with
# the verdict, the worse-direction loss %, and "device interface -> device
# interface" (space-separated, matching the demo's annotation style), e.g.
# "Silent packet loss 17.0% srl1 ethernet-1/1 -> srl2 ethernet-1/1, both ports clean".
# All three verdicts that reach a loss_pct (silent packet loss, healthy link,
# inconclusive-with-partial-loss) only get there via the compute-verdict
# branch that already ruled out port errors on either end, so "both ports
# clean" is always accurate here. Verdicts with no loss figure (telemetry
# missing, not enough traffic, errors on one/both ends, cable missing in
# NetBox) keep the original "[verdict] near/iface <-> far/iface" form since
# there is no loss number to show.
loss_pct = figures.get('loss_pct') if isinstance(figures, dict) else None
annotation = None
if loss_pct:
    loss_a = loss_pct.get('near_to_far')
    loss_b = loss_pct.get('far_to_near')
    candidates = []
    if loss_a is not None:
        candidates.append((loss_a, f"{near_device} {near_interface} -> {far_device} {far_interface}"))
    if loss_b is not None:
        candidates.append((loss_b, f"{far_device} {far_interface} -> {near_device} {near_interface}"))
    if candidates:
        worst_pct, worst_dir = max(candidates, key=lambda c: c[0])
        verdict_label = (verdict[0].upper() + verdict[1:]) if verdict else verdict
        annotation = f"{verdict_label} {worst_pct:.1f}% {worst_dir}, both ports clean"

if annotation:
    summary_text = annotation
else:
    summary_text = f"[{verdict}] {near_device}/{near_interface} <-> {far_device or '?'}/{far_interface or '?'}"

body_lines = [
    f"Silent packet loss check result: {verdict}",
    "",
    detail,
    "",
    f"Near end: {near_device} / {near_interface}",
    f"Far end:  {far_device or 'unknown'} / {far_interface or 'unknown'}",
    "",
    "Figures (rates, packets/sec, averaged over the last 5 minutes):",
]
for end_name in ('near', 'far'):
    fig = figures.get(end_name) if isinstance(figures, dict) else None
    if fig:
        body_lines.append(f"  {end_name}:")
        for k, v in fig.items():
            # Round every rate to one decimal and label the unit explicitly
            # rather than printing the raw float.
            if v is None:
                body_lines.append(f"    {k}: no data")
            else:
                body_lines.append(f"    {k}: {v:.1f} packets/s")
if loss_pct:
    body_lines.append("")
    near_to_far = loss_pct.get('near_to_far')
    far_to_near = loss_pct.get('far_to_near')
    near_to_far_str = f"{near_to_far:.1f}%" if near_to_far is not None else "no data"
    far_to_near_str = f"{far_to_near:.1f}%" if far_to_near is not None else "no data"
    body_lines.append(f"Loss near->far: {near_to_far_str}")
    body_lines.append(f"Loss far->near: {far_to_near_str}")

body_text = "\n".join(body_lines)

set_output({
    'verdict': verdict,
    'summary_text': summary_text,
    'body_text': body_text,
    'time_epoch_ms': now_ms,
})
snippets.logic_diagram_mermaid:
flowchart TD
    in([compute-verdict.output OR cable-missing-verdict.output - whichever ran]) --> pick[pick the non-skipped result]
    pick --> hasloss{loss_pct present and a direction has a value?}
    hasloss -->|yes| worst[pick worse direction] --> ann["Verdict X.X% near iface -> far iface, both ports clean"]
    hasloss -->|no| legacy["[verdict] near/iface <-> far/iface"]
    ann --> fmtbody[format body: rates rounded .1f + packets/s, loss % rounded .1f + percent]
    legacy --> fmtbody
    fmtbody --> out([verdict, summary_text, body_text, time_epoch_ms])

snippets.name: silent-loss-build-queries
snippets.description: Builds one PromQL rate() expression per link end, covering all 6 SR Linux packet/error counters in a single query.
snippets.code:
from flowweaver_runtime import get_input, set_output

METRICS = [
    'gnmic_srl_if_stats_out_packets',
    'gnmic_srl_if_stats_in_packets',
    'gnmic_srl_if_stats_in_fcs_error_packets',
    'gnmic_srl_if_stats_in_discarded_packets',
    'gnmic_srl_if_stats_out_error_packets',
    'gnmic_srl_if_stats_out_discarded_packets',
]


def _expr(device, interface):
    names = '|'.join(METRICS)
    # Raw counters only - no rate() here. Wrapping a __name__ regex that
    # matches multiple metrics in rate() drops the __name__ label from the
    # output series, collapsing all 6 metrics onto the same labelset
    # (source, interface_name) and Prometheus rejects the vector. Instead we
    # return the bare counters as a range query and compute the rate
    # downstream per-metric from the raw samples (first/last over elapsed
    # time), after __name__ is still attached to each series.
    return '{__name__=~"' + names + '", source="' + device + '", interface_name="' + interface + '"}'


inp = get_input()
lk = inp['steps']['netbox-lookup']['output']
near_device = lk['near_device']
near_interface = lk['near_interface']
far_device = lk['far_device']
far_interface = lk['far_interface']

if not far_device or not far_interface:
    raise ValueError("build-queries reached with no far-end resolved - check the conditional edge wiring")

set_output({
    'near_device': near_device,
    'near_interface': near_interface,
    'far_device': far_device,
    'far_interface': far_interface,
    'near_expr': _expr(near_device, near_interface),
    'far_expr': _expr(far_device, far_interface),
    'start_time': 'now-5m',
    'end_time': 'now',
    'step_seconds': 60,
})
snippets.logic_diagram_mermaid:
flowchart TD
    in([steps.netbox-lookup.output: near/far device+interface]) --> chk{far end resolved?}
    chk -->|no| f([step FAILS - wiring error])
    chk -->|yes| build[build raw counter selector per end, no rate(), 6 metrics via __name__ regex, 5m range query]
    build --> out([near_expr, far_expr, start_time, end_time, step_seconds])
